note: Track improvise (voice-harmony), step 2: the two guide-tone lines over ii-V-I with a slow band, then a made-up line that lands on the 3rd or the 7th over a bossa. Rewritten from the plan exercise (ChoiceSplit3): the Stage selector that set the tempo is a move now (72 to 104), with any key beside it; the bossa keeps its own tempo (pinned), so it stays the faster of the two. The why says what holds a line together, so it no longer leans on the tempo, and the title lost its "faster".

exercise.title: Your line over ii-V-I
exercise.why: A made-up line holds together when you know where it lands, so fix the landing first, the 3rd or the 7th as the last chord arrives, and make up only the way there.

cells.text:
Press Start exercise below to start the mic and the band, at {{=bpm}}. Sing the two guide-tone lines, one note per chord: {{4}}, {{4}}, {{3}}, then {{1}}, {{7}}, {{7}}. Sing them on "ah".
Go round the chords until each note is ready before its chord arrives.
In another key the notes are new, and each line still has one drop of a half step.

Press Start exercise below to start the mic and the band, now a bossa and faster. Make up a line over the first two chords, and land on {{3}} as the last chord arrives. Sing it on any vowel.
Then aim for {{7}} instead.
Once both landings come easily, leave a bar empty now and then.
